comparison: Perfect agreement. Both recognize claims C1-C6 as established background facts about CX anatomy and function supported by prior literature. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement. Both strongly support claims C7, C14-C16 regarding genetic tool generation. OpenEval emphasizes imaging data and characterization; peer reviewers praise these as 'fantastic tools' and 'extremely valuable to the fly community.'

Strong agreement on neuropeptide expression patterns (C8, C9, C50, C51, C55, C58). OpenEval supports based on EASI-FISH data; peer reviewers call this work 'of remarkable importance' for understanding CX function. Both evaluations also overlap on C10-C12, C46-C47, C56 regarding broader neuropeptide characterization.

Agreement on neuropeptide/neurotransmitter co-expression findings (C11-C13, C20, C46, C48, C49, C56, C61-C63). OpenEval supports based on Figure 9 and EASI-FISH data; peer reviewers emphasize the importance of neurotransmitter/neuropeptide expression patterns for future CX studies.

Agreement on co-transmission findings (C13, C20, C22, C23, C48, C49). OpenEval supports based on comprehensive survey data; peer reviewers highlight the importance of neurotransmitter/neuropeptide characterization without raising concerns.

Agreement on tyramine production in PFG neurons (C17). OpenEval supports based on EASI-FISH showing Tdc2 without Tbh; peer reviewers accept this as part of the broader neurotransmitter characterization they praised.

Agreement on rare triple co-expression in FB4K neurons (C18, C19, C21). OpenEval supports based on EASI-FISH data; peer reviewers accept this as part of the important neurotransmitter expression pattern description.
Agreement on neurotransmitter co-expression patterns (C22, C23). OpenEval supports based on comprehensive survey; peer reviewers emphasize importance of this characterization work.

Agreement on receptor expression patterns (C10, C57). OpenEval supports based on EASI-FISH data showing multiple receptors with distinct patterns; peer reviewers praise the broader neuropeptide/receptor characterization.

Partial disagreement on behavioral screen completeness (C24-C28, C64-C67, C70, C84-C85). OpenEval finds claims supported by extensive behavioral data using multiple metrics and methods. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly critiques the screen as 'incomplete' and 'unfinished,' noting lack of silencing data, sleep homeostasis assessment, and concern that mild activation protocols may have missed phenotypes.

Agreement on behavioral methodology (C64-C67, C70, C84-C85). OpenEval supports the systematic approach with multiple lines, sexes, and activation methods. Peer reviewers accept the methodology itself (thermogenetic/optogenetic approaches, testing both sexes) even while critiquing the screen's completeness.

Partial disagreement on sexual dimorphism findings (C87-C96). OpenEval supports claims based on detailed behavioral data across multiple lines. Peer Reviewer 2 questions completeness of the behavioral screen overall, noting possible insufficient activation protocols that may have 'missed some phenotypes,' though doesn't specifically challenge the sexual dimorphism findings.

Agreement on acknowledging inconsistencies (C97-C98, C100-C104). OpenEval notes authors appropriately acknowledge inconsistency and refrain from strong conclusions. Peer Reviewer 2's critique of incomplete screen aligns with OpenEval's recognition of limitations, though peer review is more critical overall.

Partial disagreement on wake-promoting effects (C29-C32, C109-C112). OpenEval finds robust, reproducible effects supported by behavioral and connectivity data. Peer Reviewer 2 critiques the behavioral screen as incomplete, lacking silencing data and sleep homeostasis assessment, though acknowledges the work 'will pave the way for further studies.'

Agreement on connectivity analysis (C31-C32). OpenEval supports based on connectome data linking clock neurons to CX. Peer reviewers accept the connectivity analysis as part of the 'anatomical, molecular, and functional mapping' without raising concerns.

Agreement on receptor expression and connectivity (C33-C36). OpenEval supports based on RNA profiling and EASI-FISH data. Peer reviewers accept the molecular characterization and connectivity findings as part of the overall contribution.

Agreement on connectivity analysis (C44-C45, C68-C69, C113-C117). OpenEval supports based on hemibrain connectome data. Peer reviewers implicitly accept the connectivity analysis as part of the systematic characterization they praised.

Agreement on RNA profiling methodology (C62-C63). OpenEval supports the RNA profiling corroborating EASI-FISH findings. Peer Reviewer 1 praises the work for setting 'a high and transparent standard' for large-scale resources, with no concerns about RNA profiling methodology.

Disagreement on comparison with whole-brain data (C47). OpenEval rates this claim as UNCERTAIN due to methodological differences and indirect comparison. Peer reviewers do not specifically address this claim but generally praise the neuropeptide characterization work without noting this limitation.

OpenEval evaluates overlapping expression patterns in FB tangential neurons (C105-C108) as supported but notes difficulty assigning phenotypes to specific cell types. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates the methodological approach for selecting neuropeptides (C59-C60) as supported but notes potential to miss lowly expressed neuropeptides. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological claims.

OpenEval evaluates assessment of computational approaches (C72-C76) as supported, noting appropriate positioning of experimental FISH approach. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological considerations.
OpenEval evaluates conceptual foundations (C77-C80) as supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates acknowledgments of experimental limitations (C81-C83) as supported and appropriate. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers did critique the behavioral screen as incomplete, which aligns with some of these limitations.
